S1.why: Elliptical 'five free [cutlings]', the noun is the tiles above; genitive plural is the form after 5 (2 to 4 would take 'бесплатна').

S2.why: An invitation in the formal imperative the vocabulary uses; no limit word, no price, just carry on.

S3.s: Искористили сте свих %lld бесплатних катлинга. Они остају бесплатни и раде као и досад.
S3.back: Used-up have-you all 5 free cutlings. They stay free and work as and until-now.
S3.why: Past tense with formal 'сте'; 'као и досад' is the everyday way to say nothing changes for them; item word 'катлинг' lowercase in prose as in the vocabulary sentence.

S4.why: States the offer as a plain fact about the person's first items instead of 'you can', which reads like a sign.

S5.why: Agreement hangs on the total after 'од', so the sentence stays correct for any used count; positional placeholders keep the order safe.

S6.why: Short noun phrase for a bold row; genitive plural after a number ending in thousands.

S7.why: 'текст' and 'слике' from the vocabulary (text kind, images), in the genitive plural the numbers require.

S8.why: Serbian lists with 'и' before the last item and no comma before it; product names stay in Latin script as Apple writes them.

S9.s: Једна куповина за све уређаје пријављене на ваш Apple налог.
S9.back: One purchase for all devices signed-in onto your Apple account.
S9.why: 'пријављен на ваш Apple налог' is the vocabulary's own phrase for the account and devices; lowercase formal 'ваш' as the vocabulary writes it.

S10.why: Present tense, formal 'you'; 'само једном' is what a person says about a one-off price.

S11.s: Без претплате, без реклама и без регистрације.
S11.back: Without subscription, without ads and without registration.
S11.why: Repeating 'без' is how Serbian stresses an absence; 'регистрација' is the common word for signing up for an account.

S12.why: The wording Serbian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action, in the 2nd-person-singular imperative Serbian buttons take (like 'Настави').

S13.why: Verbal noun for an action in progress, as iOS writes busy states in Serbian, ending in the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: Button imperative like 'Настави'; 'за' plus a price is the natural 'for this much'; the one-time part is said in S10, so the button stays one line.

S15.why: Same verb as S14 so the button keeps its word when the price arrives.

S16.why: Puts it off without saying no; the common polite phrase for closing an offer.

S17.why: The label Serbian iOS gives its close buttons, imperative singular.

S18.why: 'све' covers the items and the new room at once; short, warm, a little proud, no exclamation.

S19.s: Хвала вам. Овом куповином подржавате Катлинг и човека који га сам прави.
S19.back: Thank you. With-this purchase you-support Cutling and the-person who it alone makes.
S19.why: 'човека који га сам прави' says plainly that one person makes the app; 'Катлинг' is the app's name, capitalised, distinct from the lowercase item word.

S20.s: Лепо што сте опет ту. Ваша ранија куповина је враћена.
S20.back: Nice that you-are again here. Your earlier purchase is restored.
S20.why: 'Лепо што сте опет ту' is how a Serbian greets someone back; the calque 'добро дошли назад' is avoided.

S21.why: Impersonal neuter participle, which is correct for any used count; spoken, so no final period needed.

S22.why: Same label-colon-number form as the vocabulary's count ('Катлинга: %lld'), so 1, 2, 5 and 21 all read correctly without plural rules.

S23.s: Катлинг је откључан. Места има за %@ катлинга.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Room there-is for 5.000 cutlings.
S23.why: The app's name as subject, masculine participle; the number ends in thousands so genitive plural is right.

S24.why: States the fact without a subject to blame; alert titles carry no period.

S25.s: App Store тренутно није доступан. Покушајте поново мало касније.
S25.back: App Store currently is-not available. Try again a-little later.
S25.why: 'мало касније' says 'shortly' the way people say it; App Store stays in Latin script, masculine agreement.

S26.s: App Store није потврдио ову куповину.
S26.back: App Store has-not confirmed this purchase.
S26.why: Names who did not confirm, which keeps the person out of it.

S27.s: На Apple налогу пријављеном на овом уређају нема раније куповине Катлинга.
S27.back: On Apple account signed-in on this device there-is-no earlier purchase of-Cutling.
S27.why: Reuses the vocabulary's 'пријављен' for the account on the device; 'нема' plus genitive is the plain way to say nothing was found.

S28.s: Бесплатна верзија чува %lld катлинга. Откључајте Катлинг једном и чувајте колико год желите.
S28.back: Free version keeps 5 cutlings. Unlock Cutling once and save how-much ever you-want.
S28.why: Two short sentences Siri can say; 'колико год желите' is the idiom for as many as you like.

S29.why: Compact count under the title; the noun is the list title above it, adjective agrees with the total.

K1.why: Clipped banner grammar fits one key row; the second part is what the tap does, with no final period as on a button.

M1.why: Verb-led command in the imperative Serbian Mac menus and windows use.

M2.why: Same command as M1, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Nominative plural 'катлинзи' from the vocabulary's list title, as a row label.

M4.why: 'од' is how Serbian reads a count of a total aloud; shorter than a slash would sound.

M5.why: Neuter status adjective, the same form Serbian settings use for 'Укључено'; the section is already titled Cutling.

M6.s: Једна куповина откључава Катлинг за iPhone, iPad и Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling for iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: 'за' takes the accusative, which leaves the Latin product names undeclined, as in the vocabulary's 'Катлинг за Mac'.

M7.s: Откључано за iPhone, iPad и Mac на овом Apple налогу.
M7.back: Unlocked for iPhone, iPad and Mac on this Apple account.
M7.why: Same 'за' construction as M6 so the names stay undeclined; 'Apple налог' from the vocabulary.

M8.s: Катлинг сте купили пре него што је постао бесплатан, па остаје откључан. Хвала вам.
M8.back: Cutling you-have bought before than that it became free, so it-stays unlocked. Thank you.
M8.why: Reason then result joined with 'па', the everyday connective; thanks closes as a separate short sentence.
